title: 3rd Grade Math Quiz
description: Ten questions for 3rd graders: multiplication facts, division, simple fractions and perimeter, with explanations.

questions.question: What is 7 × 8?
questions.explanation: 7 × 8 = 56. If you said 54, you may have mixed it up with 6 × 9.

questions.question: A pizza is cut into 4 equal slices. You eat 3 slices. What fraction of the pizza did you eat?
questions.explanation: You ate 3 out of 4 equal parts, which is 3/4. The fraction is (parts eaten) / (total parts).

questions.question: A rectangle is 6 cm long and 4 cm wide. What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: Perimeter adds all four sides: 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 = 20 cm. 24 cm is the area (6 × 4), not the perimeter.

questions.question: What is 9 × 6?
questions.explanation: 9 × 6 = 54. A quick check: 10 × 6 = 60, so 9 × 6 is 6 less, which is 54.

questions.question: Which fraction is bigger: 1/2 or 1/4?
questions.explanation: With the same numerator, the smaller denominator makes the bigger piece: half a pizza beats a quarter.

questions.question: A square has sides of 5 cm. What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: A square has 4 equal sides: 4 × 5 = 20 cm. 25 cm is the area, not the perimeter.

questions.question: If 3 × 4 = 12, what is 12 ÷ 3?
questions.explanation: Multiplication and division undo each other: 12 ÷ 3 = 4.

questions.question: A chocolate bar is split into 6 equal pieces. You eat 2 pieces. What fraction did you eat?
questions.explanation: 2 eaten out of 6 total pieces is 2/6.
